title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
lead: First identify whether the issue occurs on public Pages, in the local Web app, or in a native app. Check licensing, network access, setting application, and media or device support separately.

blocks.text: The Web event log, the browser’s Console and Network panels, and native error codes provide clues. Record the source, theme, changed fields, and apply action so that you can compare results. A successful build alone does not establish successful license authentication or actual playback.

rows: License error on Pages
Check that the Player license allows the public host kazuhide.github.io.
Check the dedicated public-demo license and deployment configuration. The localhost exception does not apply to Pages. Do not try to fix it by entering an account API key.
The local Web app does not start
Check that the server is running, the port is correct, and the URL is reachable. The instructions use localhost.
Open the startup URL with localhost as the host. If you use another hostname or a LAN IP address, also check the license permissions for that host.
Different behavior on 127.0.0.1
127.0.0.1 and localhost are different origins, with separate storage and CORS conditions.
Use localhost consistently for this guide’s reproduction steps. The SDK officially exempts 127.0.0.1 from authentication from version 8.86.0, but playback at that URL was not verified for this guide.
Native error 1003
The Player license request failed or was rejected. Check the application identifier, key type, and network.
Check that the Android applicationId or Apple Bundle ID matches the license permissions. Synchronize settings and rebuild. An unapproved identifier is not the only possible cause.

blocks.text: 1003 is LicenseAuthenticationFailed in the native SDKs. It is separate from DRM errors when decrypting content. Read the error definition for the target SDK rather than assuming the Web error number has the same meaning.

rows: The source loads but does not autoplay
Check whether the browser blocks autoplay with sound.
Press play inside the video. For comparison, try muted autoplay, then adjust volume and mute after playback starts.
The media URL fails, returns 404, or requires authentication
In Network, check not only the manifest but also the referenced video, audio, subtitles, and images.
Correct the URL, access permissions, authentication or expiry, and relative paths. Compare Player settings after retrieval succeeds.
The URL opens directly but fails in the Web app
Check CORS messages in Console and response headers from the media server.
Allow the app’s origin at the media server. Apply the required permissions to segments and subtitles as well as the manifest. Do not use disabled browser security as a fix.
An HTTPS page cannot fetch HTTP media
Check Console for Mixed Content messages or fetch failures after a change to HTTPS.
Serve media and its referenced resources over HTTPS for use on public pages. Do not use a local HTTP URL unchanged as a public Pages source.
An additional-media button is disabled
For the local Web app, check the required settings shown near the button for missing media environment variables.
Configure the required media URLs using the sources, audio, subtitles, and thumbnails chapter. Pages uses bundled media.
Audio/subtitle lists are missing, or a track is undefined
Check that loading has completed, that the source has tracks, and that the theme provides a selection menu. An empty value alone does not identify the cause.
Compare with a configured VOD + Multi-audio or VOD + Subtitles source. Use a theme such as Default or Premiere and select a track after loading completes.

blocks.text: Applying settings and meeting display conditions

rows: A Player Config change has no visible effect
Check whether the field applies immediately, reloads the source, or recreates the Player, and whether you pressed the appropriate apply button.
Apply the change as described in the Player Config chapter. Re-enter any unapplied input lost during a language switch.
An earlier source setting remains or disappears
Check whether the action reloads the source or selects a preset again.
A reload preserves other applied overrides. A source button or recommendation selection clears sourceOverrides, even when selecting the same preset.
A UI setting does not change the appearance
Check the field’s conditions, such as theme, subtitle format, markers, or the first playback.
Check the UI settings and external playback chapter. The 60-second Pages media cannot demonstrate snapping to sample markers at 120 seconds and beyond.
Cast, AirPlay, or PiP buttons are missing
Check browser/OS support, receivers, connection requirements, and differences between standard and custom UI.
Try a supported environment and receiver. Enabling a button in the custom UI does not guarantee availability or successful output to a real device.
A TV or VR operation described in the guide is missing
Check whether the description covers the current GUI or a code example to add.
Use the UI customization chapter to check the distinction. Examples such as SpatialNavigation and VR are not implemented screen controls.
Live rewind is unavailable
Check Allow DVR, dvrAvailable, maxTimeShift, and source loading.
Try a public live source with an available rewind window. For HLS, wait until the range is known. Increasing the buffer does not extend the retained history.
The screen shows needs PDT
Check wall-clock information from the stream and the device clock. These are separate conditions from relative time and the DVR window.
Use media with wall-clock information. Do not interpret unavailable wall-clock latency as zero; distinguish it from relative position and distance from the SDK’s live edge.
There is no server-query panel on Pages
Pages serves static files and has no server to process account aggregate queries.
The panel is intentionally hidden. Check the current playback in the QoE section. Configure the local development server if aggregate queries are needed.
Analytics seems disabled because the query panel is missing
The query UI and playback collector are separate features.
Public Pages shows a collection notice and sends events through a collector configured with a dedicated license. Verify successful sending and dashboard aggregation separately.

blocks.text: Why do live controls change when an event ends?

A finished event can become a finite VOD presentation. HLS can signal that no more segments will be added with EXT-X-ENDLIST; DASH can change a dynamic manifest to a finite static presentation. When the app observes a finite, positive duration, it switches to VOD controls and disables live rewind/return commands. Finalization does not create more rewind history, and a theme named Live does not make a VOD source live.
Why can Apple still report live after HLS ends?

On Apple Player 3.128.0, a completed HLS Source can keep isLive = true and an infinite duration. The app records PlaybackFinished for the current Source that loaded as live, shows ended-live and disables its live commands. The shared Live and Sports UIs hide their LIVE controls and retain Replay. Replaying the same Source preserves this completion state; a new load clears it. The app does not change the SDK getters.

To read the final manifest as finite VOD, keep the URL and player settings, change only Title under Configure source and playback, and Apply when the action says Reload source. This loads a new Source on the same Player and URL and resets playback position. Reloading is a separate action from finishing or replaying the original Source.
Why does a finished clip still have clock-based positions?

A source that used wall-clock timestamps while live can keep that origin after becoming finite VOD. The shared UI displays and seeks relative to the seekable-range start. In API code, use getSeekableRange().start + the desired clip offset as the seek target, then wait for a fresh Seeked event and inspect getCurrentTime("relativetime"). An absolute seek(10) can instead be clamped to the start. The live-only Sports clock is hidden outside live playback.

blocks.title: Rapid quick-seek clicks
blocks.text: Player UI 4.23.0 updates its pending target after the SDK Seek notification. Two rapid backward clicks before that notification can request the same position. If checking a precise movement, wait for Seeked and confirm the result before the next action.

When sharing findings, report the target SDK, source type, reproduction steps, error codes, and retrieval results without including key values, authentication headers, personal information, or private media URLs.

blocks.title: Comparing playback time and the display
blocks.text: Standard Web time labels omit fractional seconds; Player state’s time (rel) includes a decimal place. The shared VOD controls use the seekable-range start as their origin, which need not match the SDK’s relative-clock origin. Compare values with the same origin and precision. Seeked confirms that seeking has finished, but the display can refresh afterwards. Read the SDK position after the event and wait for the time readout to catch up. The VOD seek bar’s left/right keys calculate the next position from the SDK clock, rounded down to whole seconds, rather than the previous display.
